references.text: The first leader, Nahshon from the tribe of Judah, gave the same offering with a silver plate, a silver bowl, and fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering. This shows the repeated pattern of the tribes' gifts.
Nethanel from the tribe of Issachar gave identical gifts: a silver plate weighing 130 shekels and a silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil.
The description of the sanctuary vessels and bowls made for the tabernacle, including the materials used and their role in worship services.
The sanctuary shekel is mentioned as the standard unit of weight, the same one used to measure the silver objects in this verse.
The regulations for grain offerings consisting of fine flour mixed with oil, which correspond to the contents of the silver plate and bowl given as gifts.
A summary of all the tribes' gifts, including the total number of silver plates and silver bowls presented at the dedication of the tabernacle.
